historical_growth.growth_rate_source: current run-rate (H1 2026 revenue +14.7% YoY, Q2 2026 +23% YoY) and FY2026 guidance (organic net revenue growth raised to mid-to-high teens), decelerating over the 10-year base-case path toward a ~4.5% terminal rate -- not the trailing 3/5yr equity or revenue CAGR alone
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (14.0% 3yr / 8.9% 5yr) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (6.0% 3yr / 6.6% 5yr) in both windows. The 3yr equity CAGR is distorted by a low FY2022 base (EBITDA margin collapsed to 16.6% that year on a significant one-off/impairment item visible in the Q2 2022 net-income swing to -$184.5M quarterly), so retained-earnings compounding off that trough overstates sustainable growth capacity. EPS CAGRs are similarly distorted by the same FY2022 trough (3yr EPS CAGR of 68% is not repeatable). Revenue CAGR and the current TTM/H1 2026 acceleration are used as the more reliable growth anchors instead; FCF CAGRs are not used as the anchor at all because reported FCF is lumpy year to year on clearing-related working-capital swings (FY2020's $1,411M reported FCF was a COVID volatility-spike outlier).

scenario_narratives.base: SPX/VIX exclusive licensing moat plus structural 0DTE retail growth (PDT repeal catalyst) sustain the guided mid-to-high-teens FY2026 growth, decelerating to a ~4.5% terminal rate as the base matures; Data Vantage's recurring international subscription growth stabilizes the mix; the strategic realignment delivers guided cost savings and a modest margin step-up to 37%.
scenario_narratives.bull: 0DTE/retail adoption compounds well past current guidance across more products and geographies; Data Vantage international expansion (Cboe Global Cloud) scales faster than guided; realignment savings plus new product launches (volatility/thematic index suite, crypto derivatives) sustain higher growth for longer and push margin toward 40%.
scenario_narratives.bear: A sustained low-volatility regime compresses the highest-margin Options segment for years; retail 0DTE engagement fades on sentiment or regulatory reversal; multi-listed competition (CME, ICE/NYSE, Nasdaq, MIAX) pressures non-proprietary fee capture; margin compresses to 30% and growth settles near 3% terminal, still above zero given the durable SPX/VIX moat.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Cboe is valued as an asset-light, moderately volume-cyclical exchange operator whose durable moat is the exclusive SPX/VIX index-options licensing franchise -- a legal monopoly on the most actively traded U.S. index options with no substitutable venue. Owner FCF (SBC-adjusted, interest income immaterial to strip given thin net cash) is projected from a component build over a 10-year horizon, reflecting still-decelerating growth even though margins are already near mature levels. The strategic realignment (divesting Cboe Australia, Canada, Japan equities and corporate listings, substantially complete by year-end 2026) is treated as a guided, in-progress cost and focus programme, not an unproven bet.
key_risks_to_valuation: Sustained low-volatility, low-volume market regime compressing the highest-margin Options transaction revenue
Loss, non-renewal, or successful competitor challenge to the exclusive SPX/VIX index licenses from S&P Dow Jones Indices
Retail 0DTE options volume proving more fickle than institutional flow if sentiment fades or the PDT rule is reinstated
Intensifying multi-listed options and cash-equities competition from CME, ICE/NYSE, Nasdaq and MIAX pressuring non-proprietary fee capture
Execution risk and one-time costs from the simultaneous divestitures and wind-downs comprising the 2025-2026 strategic realignment

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API; see inputs.price_as_of for timestamp and 52-week range
data_sources.financials: research/CBOE/Reports/CBOE_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL, DB-verified) for revenue/EBITDA/margin history; SEC XBRL companyconcept/companyfacts API (CIK0001374310) used directly to verify total debt, cash, diluted shares and dividends/buybacks for the latest quarters, per the data-quality flag in inputs.notes

inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL ShareBasedCompensation (cash-flow add-back, $50.4M FY2025) + equity_award_taxes KPI ($29.8M FY2025, tax withheld on net-share settlement); filer does not publish one combined adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation line, so the two are summed per method section 1(a)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:00Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 227.15-371.18
inputs.wacc_rationale: US large-cap exchange operator, USD risk-free ~4.2% (10yr UST) + ERP ~5.0% x beta ~0.9-1.0 (stable, asset-light, moderately volume-cyclical) = cost of equity ~8.7-9.2%; net-cash balance sheet (net cash $832M) means WACC ~= cost of equity, lightly pulled down by cheap fixed-rate senior notes. Base 8.5%, bull 7.5% (multiple-expansion-free discount for lower risk), bear 10.5% (volume-cyclicality risk premium).
inputs.lease_treatment: not material -- Cboe's operating leases (office space) are immaterial to consolidated capex/FCF for an exchange/data business; no lease adjustment applied
inputs.nci_treatment: none -- Cboe has no material noncontrolling interests in the consolidated statements
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF (routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md -- operating company, exchange operator with genuine free cash flow, not a bank/REIT/LIC; no financial-exchange-specific row exists in the routing table and none is needed, since Cboe is asset-light and generates real owner FCF rather than holding deposits or fair-valuing investment property). First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry, no prior DCF/Drivers file). DATA-QUALITY FLAG: CBOE_Metrics.csv TotalDebt for Q1/Q2 2026 ($2,092.9M/$2,093.4M) does not reconcile to SEC XBRL LongTermDebt ($1,443.4M/$1,443.8M), which has been essentially flat near $1,450M face value since FY2022 -- the CSV figure looks like a parser/adjudication artifact (possibly a duplicated current+noncurrent debt tag or an unrelated liability picked up as debt). This DCF uses the XBRL-verified total_debt of $1,443.8M and cash of $2,276.2M (net cash $832.4M), NOT the CSV's TotalDebt column; the CSV should be corrected via `make fix` before the next research pass on this ticker. Net cash ($832M) is well under 1x the owner-FCF base (~$1.5-1.9B), so interest income is immaterial to strip per the >1x materiality rule -- included at $49.4M FY2025 in reported_fcf/last_fcf reconciliation above for full auditability, but NOT deducted from the projected forward FCF stream (see projections). Base revenue uses TTM (Q3'25-Q2'26 = FY2025 + H1'26 - H1'25 = $5,061.3M) rather than FY2025 ($4,714.2M) because H1 2026 revenue grew 14.7% YoY (Q2 alone +23% YoY) on record options volumes following the June 2026 PDT-rule repeal, and management has repeatedly raised FY2026 organic growth guidance to mid-to-high teens -- anchoring to stale FY2025 would understate the current run-rate materially. Historical growth CAGRs (revenue, equity, EPS) are still reported on FY-basis per section 1c for comparability. EBITDA margin already near mature levels (33.7% FY2025, 38.3% H1 2026) reflecting operating leverage and the mix shift toward higher-margin Options/Data Vantage revenue as the strategic realignment divests lower-margin non-core businesses (Cboe Australia, Canada, Japan equities, corporate listings) -- base case margin ramps modestly from 35% to a 37% mature level, not the flat-forward trap the method warns against, because the realignment is a stated, guided cost programme ($20-25M savings) rather than an assumed improvement. SBC is a small, stable ~1.7% of revenue (FY2025) for this exchange operator -- far below a typical tech name -- held roughly flat with a slight decline glide. Deferred revenue is negligible (0.15% of revenue), so working-capital capture is set near zero; this is a transaction-fee/subscription business without material prepayment float. Cash tax rate approximated at ~27-32% over FY2023-2025 (above 21% statutory due to state taxes and non-US operations) -- no valuation-allowance distortion identified, so held near the trailing average rather than ramped.

bear.narrative: Bear case: a sustained low-volatility, low-volume regime (the risk the Analysis JSON flags as the largest single threat) compresses Options transaction revenue -- the highest-margin segment -- for several years, while retail 0DTE engagement proves more fickle than institutional flow and fades if regulation reverses (e.g., PDT rule reinstatement) or sentiment normalizes. Competition from CME, ICE/NYSE, Nasdaq and MIAX pressures fee capture in non-proprietary multi-listed products. The strategic realignment executes but produces one-time distraction costs and the divested revenue diversification is not replaced. Data Vantage growth decelerates in line with the broader slowdown rather than providing full ballast. Margin compresses toward 30% and growth settles near a ~3% terminal rate, still comfortably above the zero floor given the durable SPX/VIX moat, but with no further re-rating.

base.narrative: Base case: Cboe's SPX/VIX exclusive-license moat and the structural growth in retail 0DTE options (accelerated by the June 2026 PDT rule repeal) sustain double-digit revenue growth through the FY2026 guidance period, decelerating over the following years as the volume base matures and comps normalize, settling near a ~4.5% terminal rate anchored to nominal GDP-plus-financial-market growth. Data Vantage's recurring international subscription growth (low-teens guided) provides a stabilizing floor as transaction-fee growth decelerates. EBITDA margin expands modestly from the current 35% toward a 37% mature level as the strategic realignment (completing substantially by year-end 2026) sheds lower-margin non-core businesses and delivers the guided $20-25M of cost savings, without assuming further structural re-rating beyond what management has already guided.

bull.narrative: Bull case: 0DTE and broader retail options adoption keeps compounding well beyond current guidance as more asset classes and geographies adopt Cboe's index-options suite; Data Vantage's international expansion (Cboe Global Cloud, ex-US demand already over half of new data sales) scales faster than guided; the strategic realignment fully delivers its cost savings AND the freed-up capital/management focus drives new product launches (expanded volatility/thematic index suite, crypto derivatives via CFE) that sustain higher growth for longer. Margins expand further toward 40% as the higher-margin Options/Data mix keeps rising and non-core drag is fully removed.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 adjusted: bear weight raised to 20% (from 15%) because the single largest disclosed risk -- a sustained low-volatility/low-volume regime compressing the highest-margin Options segment -- is a real, recurring historical pattern for exchange operators (not a going-concern risk, but a genuine multi-year earnings-compression scenario), and because retail 0DTE volume (now a major driver) is a relatively untested cohort whose durability is explicitly flagged as uncertain in both the bull and bear case. Bull weight trimmed to 30% (from 35%) because the bull case requires several things to go right simultaneously (sustained 0DTE growth beyond guidance, faster Data Vantage international scaling, AND successful new product launches) rather than one dominant lever.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
